MoCo: Motion-Controlled Brain-Phenotype Differences Between Groups

Nonparametric estimation of group-specific brain-phenotype means and group differences while accounting for motion-related selection.

MoCo is an R package for brain-imaging analyses in which motion affects both data quality and inclusion in the analyzed sample. The package combines one-step estimation, flexible nuisance-function learning, optional cross-fitting, and efficient-influence-function (EIF) inference. Outcomes may be functional-connectivity edges, regional imaging measures, or other continuous brain phenotypes.

Highlights

  • A single high-level function, moco(), supports HAL, log-normal GLM, and GAMLSS models (generalized gamma, right-truncated when Delta_M is a threshold on motion) for conditional motion densities.
  • Nuisance regressions can be estimated with Super Learner or user-specified GLMs.
  • Cross-fitting and repeated cross-fitting are supported; repeated seeds are combined by averaging the estimates and the participant-level EIFs, followed by one simultaneous test.
  • If motion M = NULL, a missing data method is implemented using the data availability Delta_Y = 1, similar to Nebel et al. (2022).
  • EIF-based simultaneous confidence bands control the family-wise error rate (FWER) across multiple outcomes.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("thebrisklab/MoCo")

Then load the package:

library(MoCo)

Core dependencies, including haldensify, are installed with MoCo. The GAMLSS motion densities (density_method = "gamlss") additionally require the suggested packages gamlss and gamlss.dist:

install.packages(c("gamlss", "gamlss.dist"))

Packages corresponding to optional Super Learner wrappers—such as glmnet, ranger, and xgboost—are needed only when those learners are requested. Surface plotting additionally requires ciftiTools and Connectome Workbench.

Quick start

The bundled example data can be used for a lightweight GLM-based analysis:

library(MoCo)
data(data)

fit_glm <- moco(
  X = data$X,
  Z = data$Z,
  A = data$A,
  M = data$M,
  Y = data$Y,
  Delta_M = data$Delta_M,
  Delta_Y = data$Delta_Y,
  HAL_pMX = FALSE,
  HAL_pMXZ = FALSE,
  glm_formula = list(pMX = ".", pMXZ = "."),
  SL_library = c("SL.mean", "SL.glm", "SL.glm.interaction"),
  cross_fit = TRUE,
  cv_folds = 5,
  seed_rng = 1,
  test = TRUE,
  fwer = 0.05
)

fit_glm$est
fit_glm$adj_association
fit_glm$z_score
fit_glm$significant_regions

The main outputs are:

Output Description
est Adjusted outcome means for A = 0 and A = 1
adj_association Adjusted difference, A = 1 minus A = 0
z_score EIF-based standardized statistic for each outcome (when test = TRUE)
fwer_critical_value Simultaneous critical value for each requested FWER (when test = TRUE)
significant_regions Simultaneous-test decisions; a vector for one FWER, a matrix with one row per FWER otherwise (when test = TRUE)
density_log GAMLSS fit log, one row per seed, fold, and density (only when density_method = "gamlss"; NULL otherwise)
weight_diagnostics Density-ratio weights pMXD / pMXZ in the EIF: number, maximum, and effective-sample-size ratio, one row per seed and group

Multiple outcomes and repeated cross-fitting

For simultaneous inference, pass all outcomes in the same Y matrix. MoCo uses their joint participant-level EIF correlation structure to obtain one simultaneous critical value at each requested FWER.

When seed_rng contains several seeds, MoCo runs the full analysis once per seed and aggregates results in the following order:

  1. For each seed, compute the estimates and the participant-level EIFs.
  2. Average the group-specific estimates and adjusted differences across seeds.
  3. Average the participant-level EIFs across seeds and recompute their covariance.
  4. Compute the z-statistics from the averaged EIFs and run one simultaneous test across all outcomes.
fit_repeated <- moco(
  X = data$X,
  Z = data$Z,
  A = data$A,
  M = data$M,
  Y = data$Y,
  Delta_M = data$Delta_M,
  Delta_Y = data$Delta_Y,
  HAL_pMX = FALSE,
  HAL_pMXZ = FALSE,
  glm_formula = list(pMX = ".", pMXZ = "."),
  seed_rng = 1:10,
  fwer = c(0.05, 0.10, 0.20)
)

Within moco(), the simultaneous test is controlled by hypo_method ("mvn", the default, or "multiplier"), hypo_n_sim (100,000 draws by default), hypo_chunk_size (draws per batch, default 1,000), and hypo_seed (Monte Carlo seed, default 1, separate from the nuisance-fitting seeds).

For one outcome, the procedure reduces to a one-dimensional EIF test. For multiple outcomes, hypo_test() simulates the maximum absolute statistic from their joint EIF correlation matrix. With method = "mvn" it draws from a multivariate normal distribution with that correlation; with method = "multiplier" it uses a Gaussian multiplier bootstrap of the centered participant-level EIFs. Both target the same single-step max-|z| critical value. Its method, seed, n_sim, and chunk_size arguments control the simulation. Use hypo_test() directly only when the estimates and participant-level EIFs have already been aggregated across repeated seeds and covariance has been recomputed.

Data interface

moco() uses the following data objects:

Object Role
A Binary exposure or group indicator
X Baseline covariates
Z Post-exposure covariates used in the selection-bias adjustment
M Continuous motion measure
Y Continuous outcome vector or an n by p outcome matrix
Delta_M Indicator that motion satisfies the analysis inclusion rule
Delta_Y Indicator that the imaging outcome is observed and usable

A, X, and Z must be complete. Y may contain missing values in rows for which Delta_Y = 0. For a seed-based analysis, a seed-to-self outcome column may be entirely missing; MoCo restores that position as NA in its outputs.

Delta_M is required and must be 0 when M is missing. A motion threshold is applied by defining Delta_M directly, for example Delta_M = as.numeric(M < 0.2); the former thresh argument has been removed, and moco() stops with a message if it is supplied. The definitions of Delta_M and Delta_Y should be prespecified and reported with the analysis.

The motion densities conditional on Delta_M = 1 are fitted on the participants with Delta_M = 1 and evaluated at every observed M, including participants with Delta_M = 0. Outside the range of M among the Delta_M = 1 training participants the density is set to zero (GLM, HAL, and untruncated GAMLSS). With density_method = "gamlss" and Delta_M_threshold = c, the densities are right-truncated at c and are zero for M >= c. Delta_M need not be determined by M alone (for example, a minimum number of frames after censoring).

When motion is unavailable, set M = NULL (and optionally X = NULL) and supply Delta_M; participants with Delta_M = 0 are then treated as missing, as in Nebel et al. (2022).

Choosing a motion-density model

MoCo estimates two conditional motion densities, each in two versions:

  • pMX: a density conditional on A and X, fitted on Delta_Y = 1;
  • pMXZ: a density conditional on A, X, and Z, fitted on Delta_Y = 1;
  • pMXD and pMXZD: the same densities among participants with Delta_M = 1, fitted on Delta_M = 1 and evaluated at every observed M.

Choose their estimators with density_method ("hal", "glm", or "gamlss"), or with the switches HAL_pMX and HAL_pMXZ. HAL_pMX controls pMX and pMXD; HAL_pMXZ controls pMXZ and pMXZD. The default density_method = NULL keeps the HAL_pMX/HAL_pMXZ behavior; a supplied density_method overrides them.

Method Configuration Use case
HAL HAL_pMX = TRUE, HAL_pMXZ = TRUE (default), or density_method = "hal" Flexible conditional-density estimation with minimal distributional structure (slower, nonparametric)
GLM HAL_pMX = FALSE, HAL_pMXZ = FALSE and glm_formula$pMX/pMXZ, or density_method = "glm" Parsimonious log-normal motion-density model (faster, but most restrictive parametric assumptions)
GAMLSS density_method = "gamlss", with gamlss_options and Delta_M_threshold Flexible distributional regression for positive motion values (faster than HAL, semiparametric)

Methods may be combined, for example HAL_pMX = TRUE with HAL_pMXZ = FALSE, or density_method = c(pMX = "hal", pMXZ = "gamlss"), although using the same method for both is generally easier to interpret and diagnose.

Highly adaptive lasso

HAL is the default motion-density method. Its basis-function construction and regularization path can be controlled with HAL_options, which is passed to haldensify::haldensify():

fit_hal <- moco(
  X = data$X,
  Z = data$Z,
  A = data$A,
  M = data$M,
  Y = data$Y,
  Delta_M = data$Delta_M,
  Delta_Y = data$Delta_Y,
  HAL_pMX = TRUE,
  HAL_pMXZ = TRUE,
  HAL_options = list(
    max_degree = 3,
    lambda_seq = exp(seq(-1, -10, length = 100)),
    num_knots = c(1000, 500, 250)
  )
)

Log-normal GLM

For GLM motion densities, set HAL_pMX = FALSE and HAL_pMXZ = FALSE and specify the right-hand side of the pMX and pMXZ models. A value of "." uses all available predictors for the corresponding density. The same formula is used for pMX and pMXD (and for pMXZ and pMXZD). density_method = "glm" is equivalent; the density formulas then default to ".":

fit_glm <- moco(
  X = data$X,
  Z = data$Z,
  A = data$A,
  M = data$M,
  Y = data$Y,
  Delta_M = data$Delta_M,
  Delta_Y = data$Delta_Y,
  HAL_pMX = FALSE,
  HAL_pMXZ = FALSE,
  glm_formula = list(pMX = ".", pMXZ = ".")
)

GAMLSS

GAMLSS is useful when a log-normal motion model is too restrictive. density_method = "gamlss" fits all four motion densities with gamlss::gamlss(), once per training fold, using the generalized gamma (GG) family. GG has a location (mu), a scale (sigma), and a shape (nu) parameter and contains the log-normal as the special case nu = 0. All observed M must be positive.

When Delta_M is a threshold on motion, Delta_M = as.numeric(M < c), the Delta_M = 1 sample is cut at c. Supply Delta_M_threshold = c so that pMXD and pMXZD are fitted with a GG right-truncated at c (see ?GGtr). An untruncated GG fitted to a sample cut at c often fails to converge or gives a badly biased density. If Delta_M_threshold is omitted while every Delta_M = 1 participant has lower motion than every Delta_M = 0 participant, moco() warns:

Delta_M looks like a threshold on M: every participant with Delta_M = 1 has M <= 0.1989 and every
participant with Delta_M = 0 and observed M has M >= 0.2001. If Delta_M = as.numeric(M < c), set
Delta_M_threshold = c so that pMXD and pMXZD are fitted with a right-truncated GG. ...

When Delta_M is a quality-control rule that is not a cut on M (for example, a minimum number of frames after censoring), leave Delta_M_threshold = NULL.

fit_gamlss <- moco(
  X = data$X,
  Z = data$Z,
  A = data$A,
  M = data$M,
  Y = data$Y,
  Delta_M = data$Delta_M,
  Delta_Y = data$Delta_Y,
  density_method = "gamlss",
  Delta_M_threshold = 0.2,
  gamlss_options = list(
    mu = "linear",
    sigma = "1",
    nu = "1"
  ),
  cross_fit = TRUE,
  cv_folds = 5,
  test = TRUE,
  fwer = c(0.05, 0.20)
)

GAMLSS options

All entries of gamlss_options are optional:

Entry Description
family "GG", the generalized gamma (the only family currently supported); default "GG"
mu "linear" (A, X, and, for pMXZ/pMXZD, Z entering linearly; default), "smooth" (the same, with pb() on the continuous covariates), or a one-sided formula
sigma "linear" (default), "smooth", "1" (intercept only), "A" (group only), or a one-sided formula
nu "1" (constant nu, estimated; default) or 0 (nu fixed at 0, i.e. a log-normal density with the mu and sigma models above)
smooth Names of the continuous covariates that get pb() when mu or sigma is "smooth"; NULL (default) uses every numeric covariate with more than 10 distinct values
formula Optional per-density formulas, list(pMX = , pMXD = , pMXZ = , pMXZD = ), each a list(mu = , sigma = , nu = ) of one-sided formulas (nu may be 0); overrides the settings above for that density
method Fitting algorithms tried in order until one converges, any of "RS", "CG", "mixed"; default c("RS", "CG", "mixed")
n.cyc, c.crit Maximum number of outer cycles (default 500) and convergence criterion (default 0.001), passed to gamlss.control()
nu0_fallback TRUE (default): if no algorithm converges with nu estimated, refit with nu fixed at 0
clamp FALSE (default); TRUE clamps the continuous covariates of prediction rows to each density’s training range
trace FALSE (default); TRUE prints the gamlss iterations

For example, gamlss_options = list(mu = "smooth", smooth = c("X2", "Z2")) gives the location model A + X1 + pb(X2) + X3 + Z1 + pb(Z2) + Z3 + Z4 for pMXZ, and formula = list(pMXZ = list(mu = ~ A + X1 + pb(X2) + Z2, sigma = ~ A)) sets the pMXZ model directly. With nu = 0 and sigma = "1", the GAMLSS fit is essentially the log-normal GLM.

Each density is fitted with the algorithms in method, in order, until one converges. If none converges with nu estimated and nu0_fallback = TRUE, the fit is repeated with nu fixed at 0. If that also fails, the log-normal GLM density is used for that component, with a warning. The algorithm used, whether nu was fixed, truncation, convergence, the number of iterations, the fitted nu, the sample size, and whether a fallback was needed are recorded for each seed, fold, and density in density_log. weight_diagnostics summarizes the density-ratio weights pMXD / pMXZ that enter the EIF, and moco() warns when their effective-sample-size ratio is below 0.1 for either group.

Tutorial: an ABIDE-like seed-based analysis

The bundled data contain 400 simulated participants and reproduce the layout of a seed-based analysis motivated by the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE). The seed is the default mode network (DMN), and the outcomes represent its Fisher-z-transformed functional connectivity with networks from the Yeo seven-network parcellation.

library(MoCo)
data(data)
str(data)

The simulated objects are:

  • A: diagnostic group, coded 1 for ASD and 0 for non-ASD;
  • M: mean framewise displacement;
  • Delta_M: motion inclusion, with high motion defined in the simulation as mean FD greater than 0.2;
  • Delta_Y: imaging-data availability and quality;
  • X: sex, age, and handedness;
  • Z: ADOS, full-scale IQ, stimulant medication, and nonstimulant medication;
  • Y: an n by 7 functional-connectivity matrix.

The seventh column of Y is the seed-to-self position and is therefore entirely NA. Rows with Delta_Y = 0 are also missing because their imaging outcomes are unavailable. The simulated group differences are zero for the first four outcomes, -0.0485 for the fifth, and -0.0682 for the sixth.

Log-normal GLM

For a fast illustration, fit log-normal GLM motion densities and a compact Super Learner library:

fit_abide <- moco(
  X = data$X,
  Z = data$Z,
  A = data$A,
  M = data$M,
  Y = data$Y,
  Delta_M = data$Delta_M,
  Delta_Y = data$Delta_Y,
  SL_library = c("SL.mean", "SL.glm", "SL.glm.interaction"), 
  glm_formula = list(pMX = ".", pMXZ = "."),
  HAL_pMX = FALSE,
  HAL_pMXZ = FALSE,
  cross_fit = TRUE,
  cv_folds = 5,
  seed_rng = 1,
  test = TRUE,
  fwer = 0.05
)

The adjusted means are stored in est. The first row represents A = 0, the second represents A = 1, and the structural seventh column is restored as NA:

round(fit_abide$est, 4)
# est_A0 -0.2191 -0.1640 -0.1819  0.0528  0.0399  0.0862 NA
# est_A1 -0.2192 -0.1617 -0.1809  0.0491 -0.0079  0.0167 NA

The adjusted group differences are:

round(fit_abide$adj_association, 4)
# -0.0001  0.0024  0.0010 -0.0037 -0.0478 -0.0696 NA

The EIF-based test results are:

round(fit_abide$z_score, 4)
# -0.0052  0.0879  0.0404 -0.1538 -1.9283 -3.3178 NA

fit_abide$significant_regions
# FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE TRUE NA

The numerical output above is illustrative; results may vary slightly with R, dependency, and numerical-optimization versions.

GAMLSS

The same analysis with GAMLSS motion densities replaces HAL_pMX, HAL_pMXZ, and the density formulas in glm_formula with density_method = "gamlss". In the simulation Delta_M = 1 exactly when M < 0.2, so Delta_M_threshold = 0.2 fits the two densities on Delta_M = 1 (pMXD, pMXZD) with a GG right-truncated at 0.2. All covariates enter the location linearly, and the scale is constant because the sample is small:

fit_abide_gamlss <- moco(
  X = data$X,
  Z = data$Z,
  A = data$A,
  M = data$M,
  Y = data$Y,
  Delta_M = data$Delta_M,
  Delta_Y = data$Delta_Y,
  SL_library = c("SL.mean", "SL.glm", "SL.glm.interaction"),
  density_method = "gamlss",
  Delta_M_threshold = 0.2,
  gamlss_options = list(mu = "linear", sigma = "1", nu = "1"),
  cross_fit = TRUE,
  cv_folds = 5,
  seed_rng = 1,
  test = TRUE,
  fwer = 0.05
)

round(fit_abide_gamlss$est, 4)
# est_A0 -0.2167 -0.1620 -0.1732  0.0514  0.0465  0.0866 NA
# est_A1 -0.2121 -0.1481 -0.1700  0.0734  0.0020  0.0252 NA

round(fit_abide_gamlss$adj_association, 4)
#  0.0046  0.0139  0.0032  0.0220 -0.0445 -0.0615 NA

round(fit_abide_gamlss$z_score, 4)
#  0.1422  0.4984  0.1020  0.6123 -1.9095 -2.9246 NA

fit_abide_gamlss$significant_regions
# FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE TRUE NA

The fit of each density in each fold is recorded in density_log (20 rows here: 5 folds by 4 densities); all fits converged with RS, without a fallback:

head(fit_abide_gamlss$density_log[, c("fold", "density", "method", "truncated", "converged", "nu", "n")], 4)
#   fold density method truncated converged      nu   n
# 1    1     pMX     RS     FALSE      TRUE  0.0110 297
# 2    1    pMXD     RS      TRUE      TRUE -0.9506 198
# 3    1    pMXZ     RS     FALSE      TRUE -0.0596 297
# 4    1   pMXZD     RS      TRUE      TRUE  1.4645 198

fit_abide_gamlss$weight_diagnostics
#   seed group   n max_weight ess_ratio
# 1    1    A0 243      2.100     0.658
# 2    1    A1 129     18.904     0.263

Other models are set in the same list, globally or per density. For example, nu = 0 with sigma = "1" gives essentially the log-normal GLM above, and mu = "smooth" adds penalized splines pb() for the continuous covariates in the location model (not run):

gamlss_options = list(
  mu = "smooth", smooth = c("X2", "Z2"),
  sigma = "1", nu = "1",
  n.cyc = 500
)

GAMLSS models such as GG are better suited to large samples with skewed motion. On small samples, or when the Delta_M = 1 subsample is small or truncated, flexible models can fail to converge or move the estimates noticeably. On this example, the default sigma = "linear" (scale depending on all covariates) produced density-ratio weights above 600 and estimates far from the truth, and moco() warned about the low effective sample size. Omitting Delta_M_threshold had the same effect. Check density_log and weight_diagnostics before interpreting the results.

HAL

The same analysis with HAL motion densities uses HAL_pMX = TRUE and HAL_pMXZ = TRUE. The default HAL_options are computationally heavy; this example uses a lighter basis (second-order interactions, 50 penalty values, and at most 50 and 25 knots for main terms and interactions):

fit_abide_hal <- moco(
  X = data$X,
  Z = data$Z,
  A = data$A,
  M = data$M,
  Y = data$Y,
  Delta_M = data$Delta_M,
  Delta_Y = data$Delta_Y,
  SL_library = c("SL.mean", "SL.glm", "SL.glm.interaction"),
  HAL_pMX = TRUE,
  HAL_pMXZ = TRUE,
  HAL_options = list(
    max_degree = 2,
    lambda_seq = exp(seq(-1, -10, length = 50)),
    num_knots = c(50, 25)
  ),
  cross_fit = TRUE,
  cv_folds = 5,
  seed_rng = 1,
  test = TRUE,
  fwer = 0.05
)

round(fit_abide_hal$est, 4)
# est_A0 -0.2196 -0.1687 -0.1705  0.0443  0.0486  0.0947 NA
# est_A1 -0.2343 -0.1445 -0.1855  0.0458  0.0017  0.0235 NA

round(fit_abide_hal$adj_association, 4)
# -0.0147  0.0242 -0.0150  0.0016 -0.0470 -0.0712 NA

round(fit_abide_hal$z_score, 4)
# -0.5617  0.7729 -0.6339  0.0616 -1.9324 -3.0359 NA

fit_abide_hal$significant_regions
# FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE TRUE NA

This fit took about 13 minutes on a laptop, compared with about 5 seconds for the GLM fit; the GAMLSS fit takes about 2.5 times as long as the GLM fit. HAL fitting time grows quickly with the sample size, the number of covariates, max_degree, and num_knots, so HAL can be slow for large samples.

Comparison

Adjusted associations (adj_association), z-statistics, and simultaneous tests at FWER 0.05 for the three motion-density models on the example data (seed 1, five folds):

Outcome Truth GLM GAMLSS (truncated GG) HAL
1 0 -0.0001 (z = -0.01) 0.0046 (0.14) -0.0147 (-0.56)
2 0 0.0024 (0.09) 0.0139 (0.50) 0.0242 (0.77)
3 0 0.0010 (0.04) 0.0032 (0.10) -0.0150 (-0.63)
4 0 -0.0037 (-0.15) 0.0220 (0.61) 0.0016 (0.06)
5 -0.0485 -0.0478 (-1.93) -0.0445 (-1.91) -0.0470 (-1.93)
6 -0.0682 -0.0696 (-3.32) -0.0615 (-2.92) -0.0712 (-3.04)
Critical value 2.595 2.569 2.606
Run time 5 s about 2.5 × GLM 13 min

Bold marks outcomes significant at FWER 0.05. All three models detect the sixth outcome only and estimate the fifth and sixth differences close to the truth; HAL has larger standard errors on this small sample.

Which method?

  • Log-normal GLM: small samples or motion that is close to log-normal; fastest.
  • GAMLSS: large samples or skewed motion (GG); set Delta_M_threshold when Delta_M is a cut on motion, start with a simple sigma model, and check density_log and weight_diagnostics before interpreting the results.
  • HAL: the most flexible, with minimal distributional assumptions and the theoretical guarantees of the nonparametric estimator; slow.
  • Whichever model is used, report it with the analysis and check that the conclusions are robust to the choice.

The complete function documentation is available from R:

?moco

Complete moco() interface 
moco(
  X, Z, A, M, Y,
  Delta_M,
  Delta_Y,
  SL_library = c(
    "SL.earth", "SL.glmnet", "SL.gam", "SL.glm",
    "SL.glm.interaction", "SL.step", "SL.step.interaction",
    "SL.xgboost", "SL.ranger", "SL.mean"
  ),
  SL_library_customize = list(
    gA = NULL, gDM = NULL, gDY_AX = NULL, gDY_AXZ = NULL,
    mu_AMXZ = NULL, eta_AXZ = NULL, eta_AXM = NULL, xi_AX = NULL
  ),
  glm_formula = list(
    gA = NULL, gDM = NULL, gDY_AX = NULL, gDY_AXZ = NULL,
    mu_AMXZ = NULL, eta_AXZ = NULL, eta_AXM = NULL, xi_AX = NULL,
    pMX = NULL, pMXZ = NULL
  ),
  HAL_pMX = TRUE,
  HAL_pMXZ = TRUE,
  HAL_options = list(
    max_degree = 3,
    lambda_seq = exp(seq(-1, -10, length = 100)),
    num_knots = c(1000, 500, 250)
  ),
  density_method = NULL,
  Delta_M_threshold = NULL,
  gamlss_options = NULL,
  cross_fit = TRUE,
  cv_folds = 5,
  test = TRUE,
  fwer = 0.05,
  seed_rng = 1,
  hypo_method = "mvn",
  hypo_n_sim = 100000L,
  hypo_chunk_size = 1000L,
  hypo_seed = 1,
  ...
)

Nuisance-model components

SL_library_customize and glm_formula may configure the following nuisance functions separately:

Component Target
gA Propensity score, P(A = 1 | X)
gDM Motion inclusion, P(Delta_M = 1 | A, X)
gDY_AX Outcome observation, P(Delta_Y = 1 | A, X)
gDY_AXZ Outcome observation, P(Delta_Y = 1 | A, X, Z)
mu_AMXZ Outcome regression, E(Y | Delta_Y = 1, A, M, X, Z)
eta_AXZ Pseudo-outcome regression conditional on A, X, and Z
eta_AXM Pseudo-outcome regression conditional on A, M, and X
xi_AX Regression of eta_AXZ conditional on A and X
pMX Log-normal GLM motion density conditional on A and X (glm_formula only; also used for pMXD)
pMXZ Log-normal GLM motion density conditional on A, X, and Z (glm_formula only; also used for pMXZD)

Other controls

Argument Description
SL_library Common Super Learner library for nuisance regressions; if NULL, the libraries in SL_library_customize are used
SL_library_customize Separate libraries for gA, gDM, gDY_AX, gDY_AXZ, mu_AMXZ, eta_AXZ, eta_AXM, and xi_AX
glm_formula Right-hand-side formulas for nuisance GLMs and GLM motion densities
HAL_pMX Whether pMX and pMXD use HAL (TRUE) or the log-normal GLM (FALSE)
HAL_pMXZ Whether pMXZ and pMXZD use HAL (TRUE) or the log-normal GLM (FALSE)
HAL_options HAL basis and regularization controls (max_degree, lambda_seq, num_knots)
density_method "hal", "glm", or "gamlss" for all four motion densities, or c(pMX = , pMXZ = ); NULL (default) uses HAL_pMX/HAL_pMXZ
Delta_M_threshold With density_method = "gamlss": the cut c when Delta_M = as.numeric(M < c); pMXD and pMXZD are then right-truncated at c
gamlss_options GAMLSS specification (see GAMLSS options); NULL (default) uses the defaults
cross_fit Whether to use cross-fitting
cv_folds Number of cross-fitting folds
seed_rng Nuisance-fitting and cross-fitting seed or seeds
test Whether to run simultaneous EIF inference
fwer Requested family-wise error rates
hypo_method Critical-value simulation: "mvn" (default) or "multiplier"
hypo_n_sim Number of Gaussian draws for the simultaneous test (default 100,000)
hypo_chunk_size Draws processed per simulation batch (default 1,000)
hypo_seed Critical-value simulation seed, separate from the nuisance-fitting seeds (default 1)

Reproducibility and diagnostics

  • Use named columns in X and Z, especially for GAMLSS.
  • Save analysis-cohort IDs and preserve their order across outcomes and seeds.
  • Define Delta_M and Delta_Y explicitly in the analysis script.
  • Use the same outcome family when comparing simultaneous tests across methods.
  • Save the R version, package versions, learner library, fold count, and seeds.
  • Examine GAMLSS convergence and distributional diagnostics before interpreting GAMLSS-based results, and report how many fits used a fallback (density_log$fallback, density_log$method, and density_log$nu_fixed).
  • Check positivity: summarise the propensities (gA, gDM, gDY_AXZ) and the density ratios used in the influence function (weight_diagnostics), including participants with Delta_M = 0, at whose motion values the Delta_M = 1 densities are also evaluated.
  • In distributed analyses, save estimates and participant-level EIFs for every outcome and seed, then aggregate them before calculating covariance and test statistics.

Related software and resources

  • SuperLearner: ensemble learning for nuisance-function estimation.
  • haldensify: highly adaptive lasso conditional-density estimation.
  • gamlss: generalized additive models for location, scale, and shape.
  • Bethlehem et al. (2022): brain charts fitted with generalized-gamma GAMLSS, the basis of the default GG family.
  • ABIDE: motivating neuroimaging data resource for the bundled simulation.
  • Yeo seven-network parcellation: network definition used in the tutorial.
